task: Harden MLX orphan marker ownership and process identity, and reconcile MLX state after system sleep/wake

events.summary: MLX lifecycle safety and backend wake heartbeat: owner/start-time markers, native argv classification, surviving training-group witnesses, and owning documentation. Native orphan recovery is exercised only on a local test-owned MLX server; no real sleep/wake or cluster mutation.

Review follow-up reproduced classifier failures for wrapper .py.backup and argument spoofing, spaced wrapper paths, and a real disposable macOS training group whose leader exits TERM but child ignores it; the prior start-time guard rejected surviving-group cleanup.

New markers record MLX PID, owning app PID, and sysinfo process start time. Scans skip markers owned by another live app, reject start-time mismatches, and refuse termination for legacy PID-only markers. SIGTERM and SIGKILL paths compare process start time; training falls back to the PID when no process group exists. A wall/monotonic heartbeat marks training and serving slots separately for re-verification, rescans MLX markers, and emits mlx-lifecycle-wake. The next status request verifies training's MLX command line and serving's /v1/models health before clearing each flag. Review follow-up snapshots group member birth times before TERM and requires matching birth time, PGID and MLX argv before allowing group KILL after leader exit, with a final synchronous identity check immediately before signals. Wrapper matching checks the script path rather than arbitrary substrings. Process authorization now reads sysinfo native argv with explicit with_cmd Always; ps flattened text is used only by legacy diagnostic tests. All sysinfo inspection in async paths runs on blocking workers.

Lifecycle and fake-clock tests plus real macOS disposable process-group regressions passed: matching child is killed after leader exit; mismatched marker birth refuses TERM; an unverified surviving sleep child refuses KILL. Structured argv and a real unrelated report process carrying a wrapper argument are distinguished correctly.
